p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the phophohexose isomerase reaction. Starting from the top left of the diagram, there's an elongated hexagon, which represents Glucose 6-phosphate, with thickened lines at the 3 base lengths of the structure. The carbons in this structure are numbered in pink. Starting with the O at the top right-hand corner of the hexagon (and moving clockwise), 1 is to the right point, followed by 2 and 3 at the bottom points, 4 on the left corner, and 5 next to that. About halfway on the bond between the O and first carbon (at position 1), there's a dashed line. The carbon in position 1 is bonded to a H on top and OH to the bottom. The carbon in position 2 is bonded to H on top and OH on the bottom. The carbon in position 3 is bonded to OH on top and H on the bottom; the carbon in position 4 is bonded to H on top and down to OH; and the carbon in position 5 is bonded to CH2OPO3, with a minus 2 charge on it. The C in CH2OPO3 is labeled a pink 6. Below this structure is reversible arrow, labeled "Binding and opening of the ring" in a yellow box. The reversible arrow has a white number 1 in a grey circle next to it; this indicates step 1. Below the reversible arrow is a structure of a molecule, labeled "Phosphohexose isomerase." This structure also has 6 Carbons, labeled in pink numbers, from top to bottom in a vertical line. The carbon at the 1 position is double bonded to an O to the top right and bonded to a H on the left. A pink arrow juts out from the double bond to the top of the O. This first C is also bonded to a C in the 2 position, which is bonded to an OH, with the H shaded in blue, to the right, and bonded to an H, shaded in orange, to the left. A pink arrow juts out from the H to the bond between the C's in the 1 and 2 positions. From the left, the letter B, which sits on a light blue elongated parenthesis, has two small pink dots next to it and an arrow pointing from the two dots to the H shaded orange and bonded to the C in the 2 position. The C in the 2 position is also bonded down to HOCH; the C in this is marked a pink 3. HOCH is then bonded down to HCOH; this C is marked a pink 4. HCOH is bonded down to another HCOH; the C here is marked a pink 5. This HCOH is bonded down to CHCOPO3, with a minus 2 charge on. The C in this molecule is marked a pink 6. To the right of this entire structure is a reversible arrow with an H+, shaded yellow, entering the top arrow; this reversible arrow indicates step 2. Below this, there's text that reads "Proton abstraction by active-site Glu (B:) leads to cis-enediol formation." The text is in a yellow box, and the : on the B are also pink. To the right of the reversible arrow is another structure, labeled cis-Enediol intermediate. Starting from top to bottom in the vertical structure, the first C is bonded up and right to OH, whose H is shaded yellow. To the left and up, it is bonded to H. This same C is also double bonded down to another C, which is bonded to an O on the right, and the O is bonded to an H to the right. This H is shaded blue and has a red arrow jutting out from it to the C-O bond next to it. There is another red arrow that juts out from the double bond between the first and second C's, and points to an H shaded orange, connected to the B on the light blue elongated parenthesis to the left. The second C is bonded down to HOCH, which bonded down to HCOH, which is bonded down to HCOH, which is bonded down to CH2PO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. To the right of this structure is an arrow pointing to the right; this arrow has a small curved arrow coming out of it and labeled H+ and shaded blue. This arrow represents step 3, and below it, the text reads, "General acid catalysis by same Glu facilitates formation of fructose 6-phosphate." The text is in a yellow box. To the right of the arrow is another vertical structure with 6 carbons. From top to bottom, the first C is bonded up to an H, bonded right to an OH, with the H shaded yellow, and bonded left to an H shaded orange. To the left of the H shaded orange is a B with two red dots next to it on the light blue parenthesis, but the two are not bonded. The first C bonds down to another C, which double bonds to an O to the right. The second C bonds down to HOCH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2PO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. Above this structure is a reversible arrow, which represents step 4. Next to the arrow on the right is a yellow text box that rads, "Dissociation and closing of the ring." Above this is another elongated hexagon with thick lines at the 3 bases lengths. Atop the structure is an O. Moving clockwise (to the right), the O is bonded to a C, labeled a pink 2, which bonds down to OH and up to CH2OH. The C in CH2OH is labeled a pink 1. C2 bonds to C3, which bonds up to OH, down to H, and left to C4, also labeled in pink. C4 bonds up to H, down to OH and up to the left to C5 (the 5 is labeled in pink), which bonds down to H and up to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. the C in this structure is labeled a pink 6. Between the O at the top of the hexagon and the C marked 2, there is a dashed line. This structure is labeled Fructose 6-phosphate.
